name: Soy sauce (food medium)
description: Food-derived medium: metabolizable components of Soy sauce [Soy] from FooDB, plus a standard M9 mineral base. Organic components use presence-based uptake bounds; FooDB content retained. Measured compounds with no BiGG exchange are listed under uncovered.

provenance.citation: FooDB v2020-04-07 (Wishart DS et al., foodb.ca). Content sources: DTU, PHENOL EXPLORER, USDA.
provenance.notes: Organic components mapped from FooDB compounds to BiGG via InChIKey/name. Mineral base added. Bounds presence-based; foodb_content retained. Unmapped measured compounds kept in uncovered (v2 completeness fix). IMPORTANT: composition values are taken from the archived FooDB 2020-04-07 CSV data release; FooDB's live food page no longer displays this bulk composition, so it will appear empty. Verify individual compounds via the per-component cross-reference links. Underlying content was aggregated by FooDB from USDA / DTU / Phenol Explorer.
provenance.verification: expert-curated (multi-source food composition; growth-relevant profile completed, FooDB noise removed)
curation_sources: USDA FoodData Central FDC 174277 (Soy sauce made from soy and wheat, shoyu; SR-Legacy 16124) - full nutrient panel incl. sugars, amino acids, fatty acids, minerals, vitamins
Frontiers in Microbiology 2020, doi:10.3389/fmicb.2020.579808 (organic acids, sugars, ethanol in Japanese soy sauces)
Journal of Food Science 2018, doi:10.1080/10942912.2018.1497061 (organic acid quantitation: lactic, acetic, succinic, pyroglutamic)
Shodex KC-811 application note - HPLC organic-acid profile of soy sauce
Umami Information Center - free glutamate content of shoyu (782-1264 mg/100mL)
Kikkoman / Fukushima soy-sauce reviews - ethanol content of brewed koikuchi shoyu (~1.5-2.5% w/v)
provenance.curation_notes: Soy sauce is a high-salt (~15-18% NaCl; Na+ ~2.4 M) hydrolysed-protein brine. Dominant growth substrates are FREE AMINO ACIDS/peptides (glutamate first, then aspartate) as combined C+N, plus lactic acid (dominant organic acid) and residual glucose as carbon; ethanol (~2%) is a defining fermentation metabolite. The critical growth constraint is osmotic/ionic stress from the salt, so only halotolerant organisms grow. Sugars are low in plain shoyu but much higher in sweetened Chinese/amakuchi types
curation_added: L-lactic acid (dominant organic acid, was absent)
citric acid / malic acid / formic acid / pyruvic acid (trace, null)
quantitative amounts for glucose and sucrose
quantitative amounts for all free/total amino acids (glutamate dominant)
quantitative amounts for all minerals (esp. ~15-18% NaCl / Na+ ~2.4 M)
quantitative amounts for all B vitamins

curation_removed.name: Nickel
curation_removed.reason: Non-nutritive ultratrace/contaminant element, not a defined growth nutrient of soy sauce; FooDB noise.

curation_removed.name: (R)-Oxypeucedanin
curation_removed.reason: Furanocoumarin characteristic of Apiaceae (parsley/celery/parsnip); biologically implausible in a soy+wheat ferment. FooDB predicted-not-measured noise.

curation_removed.name: (±)-erythro-Isoleucine
curation_removed.reason: Non-physiological stereoisomer artifact / duplicate of L-isoleucine; FooDB predicted noise, not a distinct nutrient.

curation_removed.name: Co2+
curation_removed.reason: Free cobalt ion listed at ultratrace with no quantitation and no B12 in the matrix; FooDB noise rather than a real growth nutrient (retain only if a validated Co value appears).

basis: per 100 g (approx. per 100 mL; soy sauce density ~1.1-1.2 g/mL). Reference matrix = naturally brewed shoyu (soy + wheat).

coverage_source.definition: pct_covered_all = components / (components + unresolved ingredients) — the legacy metric, which counts pipeline-derived components as covered. pct_covered_source = source-stated components / (those + unresolved ingredients + ingredients replaced by derived components). Component classes come from tools/component_evidence_classes.tsv. A null value means the denominator was zero; it does not mean 100.
